title: Coral Outplanting Procedures
description: Comprehensive standard operating procedure for outplanting nursery-grown corals to reef restoration sites, including site preparation, fragment selection criteria, cement attachment techniques (preferred over epoxy per NOAA guidelines), proper elevation off substrate, and post-outplant monitoring schedules. This SOP ensures maximum survival rates for transplanted corals.

steps.title: Outplant Site Assessment
steps.description: Before outplanting, assess the restoration site for suitability. Evaluate substrate type (prefer hard substrate with minimal sediment), current flow patterns, light availability, depth, and distance from existing live coral communities. Avoid areas with heavy sedimentation, strong wave action, or high predator populations. Ideal sites show evidence of historical coral growth and water quality within species tolerance ranges.

steps.title: Site Suitability Checklist
steps.description: Confirm the outplant site meets these minimum requirements:
checklistItems: Hard substrate available (limestone, dead coral, concrete)
Minimal sediment accumulation on substrate
Adequate water circulation (not stagnant)
Depth appropriate for target species
Light penetration sufficient for photosynthesis
No evidence of chronic pollution or runoff
Predator pressure within acceptable limits
Not in high-traffic boat or anchor zone
Access feasible for monitoring visits
Permits and permissions obtained

steps.title: Substrate Preparation
steps.description: Prepare the outplanting substrate before introducing corals. Remove algae, sediment, and biofouling organisms from attachment points using wire brushes or scrapers. Clean an area approximately 10cm diameter for each outplant location. For artificial substrates (concrete, ceramic), ensure surfaces are fully cured (minimum 30 days) and rinsed. Mark outplant positions with numbered tags for monitoring.

steps.title: Fragment Selection for Outplanting
steps.description: Select fragments that have reached optimal size for outplanting: typically 8-15cm for branching corals and 5-10cm diameter for massive species. Fragments should show robust health, active polyp extension, and established growth for minimum 3 months in nursery. Prioritize fragments with fully healed attachment bases. Mix genets at outplant sites to ensure genetic diversity.

steps.title: Fragment Readiness Criteria
steps.description: Verify each fragment meets outplanting readiness standards:
checklistItems: Minimum size threshold met for species
No signs of disease or bleaching
Active polyp extension observed
Growth margin visible and healthy
Attachment base fully healed to plug
Fragment stable on plug (not loose)
Minimum 3 months since fragmentation
No predator damage or tissue recession
Genet and lineage documented

steps.title: Cement vs Epoxy - NOAA Recommendation
steps.description: NOAA recommends using cement-based adhesives rather than epoxy for coral attachment. Cement provides stronger long-term bonding to natural substrates, better color matching to reef substrate, and more reliable performance across temperature ranges. Epoxy should only be used when cement is impractical (underwater mixing constraints, emergency situations). Always follow manufacturer specifications for underwater-rated cements.

steps.title: Outplanting Equipment Preparation
steps.description: Gather and prepare all outplanting materials:
checklistItems: Underwater cement or hydraulic cement (mixed if applicable)
Mixing container and paddle for cement
Cement application tools (trowel, spatula)
Fragment transport containers with flow-through lids
Wire brush for substrate cleaning
Identification tags (pre-numbered and waterproof)
Cable ties or wire for tag attachment
Underwater camera for documentation
GPS unit for location recording
Site map with planned placement grid

steps.title: Cement Mixing and Application
steps.description: Mix underwater cement according to manufacturer ratios (typically 3:1 cement to water). Consistency should be thick but workable - like peanut butter. Apply a mound of cement to the cleaned substrate, pressing firmly to ensure contact. Create a slight dome shape to allow water drainage and prevent pooling around coral tissue. Work in small batches to prevent cement from setting before use.

steps.title: Fragment Attachment with Elevation
steps.description: Position the fragment on the cement mound, pressing the plug or base firmly into the cement. CRITICAL: Ensure the living tissue is elevated 2-3cm above the substrate surface. This elevation prevents sediment contact, improves water circulation around the colony, and reduces smothering risk. Angle fragments slightly into the prevailing current for optimal water flow. Hold fragment in place for 30-60 seconds until cement begins to set.

steps.title: Common Outplanting Errors to Avoid
steps.description: Do NOT press coral tissue directly against substrate - this causes immediate tissue mortality. Do NOT place corals in sediment traps or depressions. Do NOT outplant during or immediately after environmental stress events. Do NOT exceed coral air exposure time of 60 seconds during transfer. Do NOT outplant diseased or compromised fragments - they will not survive and may spread pathogens.

steps.title: Spatial Arrangement and Density
steps.description: Space outplants appropriately for species growth form. Branching corals need 30-50cm spacing to allow for growth without competition. Massive species can be placed 20-30cm apart. Consider future colony fusion potential for genetically compatible fragments. Create clusters of same-species outplants to facilitate future reproduction. Document the spatial arrangement on site maps.

steps.title: Tagging and Documentation
steps.description: Attach waterproof identification tags to each outplanted fragment using cable ties or stainless steel wire. Position tags away from coral tissue to prevent abrasion. Record the following: tag number, genet ID, species, outplant date, GPS coordinates, and depth. Photograph each outplant with tag visible. Create a site map showing all outplant locations with corresponding tag numbers.

steps.title: Post-Outplant Monitoring Schedule
steps.description: Establish and follow this monitoring schedule for outplanted corals:
checklistItems: 24-48 hours: Check attachment stability and initial stress response
1 week: Assess for disease, dislodgement, or predation
2 weeks: Evaluate recovery and polyp extension
1 month: Confirm establishment and measure any growth
3 months: Full health assessment and survival count
6 months: Growth measurement and photo documentation
12 months: Annual survival rate calculation
Annually thereafter: Long-term monitoring and reproductive assessment

steps.title: Addressing Outplant Failures
steps.description: If outplants fail within the first month, assess cause of failure: dislodgement (cement failure, wave action), predation, disease, or environmental stress. Document failure rates by location and time since outplanting. Adjust future outplanting protocols based on failure patterns. Consider seasonal timing - avoid outplanting during peak bleaching risk periods or storm seasons. Replacement outplanting may be appropriate for high-priority sites.

steps.title: Seasonal Considerations
steps.description: Optimal outplanting windows vary by region. Avoid summer months in areas prone to heat stress (Caribbean: August-October). Schedule outplanting during stable weather windows with minimal storm activity. Monitor sea surface temperature forecasts and postpone if bleaching conditions are predicted. Spring and fall typically offer the best conditions in most tropical regions. Night outplanting may be advantageous in high-traffic areas.
